RDKit FragmentMol tests 1 through 9 have OEMMPA analogs or accepted API-shape divergences based on structured fragment records.

Single-cut baseline and up-enumerated stereo records are compared row for row against a committed mmpdb 3.1.4 oracle, and match for every fixture structure. The fixture now includes the two shapes that once diverged at baseline: 1,4-disubstituted rings whose cis/trans stereo is dependent rather than independently chiral, and parent SMILES carrying a stereo tag that describes nothing. mmpdb keys its dedupe on attachment_order.variable_smiles.constant_smiles without the enumeration label, which restores the rows its frag1_indices reference defect would otherwise suppress, so that defect is unobservable at one cut. The match is a statement about the fixture, not about every input: single-cut output carries whatever the cleanup pass decided about the parent, so anything the clear_fragmentation_invalidated_stereo row records flows straight through it. The classes that row once listed as residual are now in the fixture and matched against real mmpdb output -- a ring sulfoxide, a bicyclo[2.2.2] bridgehead pair, a bridgehead and an aziridine nitrogen, three-coordinate phosphorus, and the acyclic and ring pseudo-asymmetric centres of ribitol and tropine.

Potential-stereocentre detection is exercised through the fixture: centres that survive a cut, a specified tag that is not a real centre and collapses to one achiral form, prochiral carbons that a cut desymmetrises into new centres, and the three-coordinate nitrogen shapes upstream refuses to call chiral. OEMMPA applies the same shape rule as RDKit isAtomPotentialChiralCenter, which mmpdb transcribes: four heavy neighbours always qualify, three qualify with exactly one hydrogen, and three with no hydrogen qualify only for sulfur or selenium at a sulfoxide-like valence.

Covered against real mmpdb output for every class the oracle can reach. The committed fixture tests/data/mmpdb/stereo_cases.smi carries 1,4-disubstituted rings such as C[C@H]1CC[C@@H](O)CC1, 1,3-disubstituted cyclobutanes, a ring sulfoxide C[C@H]1CC[S@](=O)CC1, a bicyclo[2.2.2] bridgehead pair, the acyclic pseudo-asymmetric centre of ribitol and the ring one of tropine, a bridgehead nitrogen, an aziridine nitrogen and a three-coordinate phosphine, alongside the lone tags and the invalid geminal E/Z marker that have to be cleared; OEMMPA reproduces every mmpdb record for all of them. A cis-fused decalin and an indolizidine are in the fixture as well, but every bond in each is a ring bond so mmpdb emits no fragmentation for either; those two, macrocyclic pairs such as 1,5-disubstituted cyclooctane, and pairs spanning a spiro junction are covered by C++ unit tests in tests/cpp/test_fragment_smiles.cpp against RDKit-derived expectations, the spiro case necessarily so because both spiro tag combinations name the same molecule in RDKit and in OEChem. OEMMPA now mirrors the RDKit rule rather than approximating it: the resolve loop of Chirality.cpp::assignStereochemistry settles every tag whose neighbours are already pairwise distinct and folds the settled handedness back into the ranks, which is what separates a pseudo-asymmetric centre, and atomIsCandidateForRingStereochem pairs the unresolved remainder within one ring system, so half a pair is still cleared. Both invariants Chirality.cpp::rerankAtoms folds in are folded in here: the tetrahedral handedness settled so far, and the class-relative geometry of every stereogenic double bond, which separates a centre whose two branches are constitutionally identical and differ only in that geometry. The bridgehead test is QueryOps.cpp::queryIsAtomBridgehead as upstream writes it -- three or more ring bonds, and every ring holding one of them overlapping some other such ring in at least two bonds, not the looser two-rings-sharing-more-than-two-atoms reading -- over a ring set of every shortest cycle through each ring bond with ties kept, which is what makes both faces of a strained cage visible. Measured with benchmarks/measure_stereo_cleanup_parity.py against RDKit's parse-time cleanup over 8000 stereo-bearing structures of the public SureChEMBL corpus, read by consuming 6 row groups in order and scanning the 40604 rows in them that pass the provenance filters: 7997 agree, 0 dropped stereo, 0 extra tags kept, 3 configurations differ, 0 parse failures, down from the 222 dropped-stereo cases the previous rule left. The limit counts stereo-bearing rows rather than rows considered, so raising it always widens the measured population. No metal complex needed excluding: all 53 metal- or metalloid-bearing structures in the measured set agree, including the gold thiolate OC[C@H]1O[C@H](S[Au])[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O and the platinum chelate O=C1O[Pt]2(N[C@@H]3CCCC[C@H]3N2)OC1=O. None of the three configuration differences is a cleanup difference: each reproduces on a plain OESmilesToMol then OECreateIsoSmiString round trip with no OEMMPA code in the loop, and each already differs from RDKit there. SureChEMBL 3747 and 18208 are shape (1) below -- OEChem parses 4 and 3 tetrahedral tags respectively, writes the same number back, and the written string reads as [C@@H] where the input read [C@H] at the carbon next to the tagged quinuclidine nitrogen. SureChEMBL 20599 is shape (4) -- OEChem parses 4 specified CisTrans bonds and writes a string carrying none, so re-reading it finds 0. The residual class is entirely OEChem-side, in canonical stereo perception and in hydrogen suppression; four shapes are confirmed. (1) A stereo-tagged quinuclidine bridgehead nitrogen inverts the neighbouring ring carbon on a bare parse-and-write round trip (SureChEMBL 3747 and 18208); removing the nitrogen tag makes the round trip exact. (2) Three-coordinate phosphorus carrying an implicit hydrogen loses its tag when OESuppressHydrogens drops the materialised H, so C[P@H]CC renders as CCPC; rendering the same molecule without suppression matches RDKit. (3) In 1,3,5,7-tetrasubstituted adamantane OEChem distinguishes 3 canonical forms of the 16 tag combinations where RDKit distinguishes 8. (4) In conjugated C=N/C=C macrocycles RDKit keeps the ring double-bond directions while OEChem's bond IsChiral() clears them (SureChEMBL 20599); the bond branch still keys on IsChiral() by adjudication and is unchanged. None of the four is a tag-retention error, and OEMMPA adds no serialization workaround for any of them; they are toolkit defects to raise with OpenEye. The status stays mixed rather than matched while any of them still shows up in the measurement.

Parents whose stereo tag describes nothing (C[C@H](C)CO, a tag on a carbon carrying two identical methyls) are in the fixture and match record for record and label for label. RDKit clears such a tag while parsing, so everything downstream in mmpdb works on the normalised parent; OEMMPA reproduces that by normalising a copy of the parent before cut selection, which restores both the achiral baseline records and the up-enumerated records the phantom tag previously suppressed.

Created-stereocentre up-enumeration matches mmpdb for every enumerating fixture structure. N,N-dialkylamine and N,N-dialkylsulfonamide motifs are in the fixture rather than excluded from it: a cut that leaves a three-coordinate nitrogen with no hydrogen creates no stereocentre, because the shape rule OEMMPA now shares with mmpdb is_potential_chiral_center admits three neighbours and no hydrogen only for sulfur and selenium.

Ring-constrained and exocyclic E/Z geometry is verified against the oracle. Acyclic stereogenic double bonds are now in fixture scope as reference defect 5: mmpdb asymmetric begin/end bond-direction transfer inverts exactly one of the two cuts flanking such a bond, so the oracle itself is wrong there. The three acyclic alkene fixtures pin that divergence through allowlist rows that test_defect_5_rows_agree_with_rdkit_fragment_on_bonds binds to a single cut rather than through prose: the row's fragment pair must be reproduced by exactly one bond matching mmpdb's own default cut SMARTS, that bond must flank an alkene RDKit perceives, the mmpdb-surplus row must be that same cut with the geometry inverted, and every row must be one corner of a complete two-orientation, two-direction quartet.

Explicit design difference. The mmpdb fragment command never produces hydrogen fragmentations; only transform and predict call this surface, and only they emit its `[*][H]` _hydrogen_cut_smiles constant. The committed oracle therefore contains none, and a structural test (a projected fragment with no heavy atom) pins the absence so it cannot become an unnoticed coverage gap.
